record.paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
record.original_question: For n >= 3, construct an entire function F of n complex variables, a nonzero direction b = (b1,...,bn), and a positive continuous function L such that every one-variable slice t -> F(z0 + tb) has bounded l_z0-index for l_z0(t) = L(z0 + tb), while the full function F(z) has unbounded L-index in direction b.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 3$. For an entire function $F : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$, a nonzero direction vector $\mathbf{b} = (b_1, \dots, b_n) \in \mathbb{C}^n \setminus \{0\}$, and a positive continuous function $L : \mathbb{C}^n \to (0, \infty)$, recall the following.

(a) The function $F$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists a nonnegative integer $m$ such that for every $z \in \mathbb{C}^n$,
$$\frac{|\partial_{\mathbf{b}}^k F(z)|}{k!\, L(z)^k} \le \max_{0 \le j \le m} \frac{|\partial_{\mathbf{b}}^j F(z)|}{j!\, L(z)^j} \quad \text{for all } k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},$$
where $\partial_{\mathbf{b}} F(z) = \sum_{i=1}^n b_i \frac{\partial F}{\partial z_i}(z)$ is the directional derivative. The smallest such $m$ is the $L$-index of $F$ in the direction $\mathbf{b}$.

(b) For each fixed $z_0 \in \mathbb{C}^n$, the slice function $g_{z_0}(t) = F(z_0 + t\mathbf{b})$ is an entire function of one complex variable $t \in \mathbb{C}$. Set $\ell_{z_0}(t) = L(z_0 + t\mathbf{b})$. The slice $g_{z_0}$ is said to have bounded $\ell_{z_0}$-index if there exists a nonnegative integer $m_{z_0}$ such that
$$\frac{|g_{z_0}^{(k)}(t)|}{k!\, \ell_{z_0}(t)^k} \le \max_{0 \le j \le m_{z_0}} \frac{|g_{z_0}^{(j)}(t)|}{j!\, \ell_{z_0}(t)^j} \quad \text{for all } t \in \mathbb{C},\ k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}.$$

Construct an explicit triple $(F, \mathbf{b}, L)$ with $n \geq 3$ such that every slice $g_{z_0}$ has bounded $\ell_{z_0}$-index (the bound $m_{z_0}$ being allowed to depend on $z_0$), while $F$ does not have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$.
artifact.category_tag: Entire functions of bounded L-index in direction
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous two-variable counterexample is known: the function $F(z_1,z_2) = \cos\sqrt{z_1 z_2}$ has bounded index on every slice yet unbounded index in any complex direction. Whether such a construction has been carried out for $n \ge 3$ with the slicewise-bounded $\ell_{z_0}$-index condition stated above is not confirmed in the literature accessible via web search; recent works on slice holomorphic functions of bounded $L$-index in direction develop the theory but do not state a definitive resolution of this construction problem.

status_evidence.title: Slice Holomorphic Functions in Several Variables with Bounded L-Index in Direction
status_evidence.snippet: F(z_1,z_2)=cos sqrt(z_1 z_2) is of unbounded index in any complex direction b in C^2\{0}, but F(z_1^0 + b_1 t, z_2^0 + b_2 t) is of bounded index for every given z_1^0, z_2^0.
status_evidence.claim: The n=2 analogue is solved by an explicit example; higher-dimensional construction is referenced as a separate problem.

status_evidence.title: Entire function of bounded and unbounded index in direction
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexample demonstrating slice holomorphy with bounded slice index does not imply bounded index in direction.
status_evidence.claim: Existing counterexamples are in two variables; an n>=3 analogue is requested as an open construction.
